clue.text: Chisel cast by European artist

indicators.note: metal that is cast is melted and poured into a new shape, so the letters are remoulded

parts.note: the six letters of chisel rearranged
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A sculptor's chisel, cast in bronze, made by a European artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European artist' reads as one phrase, but European only supplies its abbreviation; Egon Schiele was an Austrian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Egon Schiele was an Austrian expressionist painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Clumsy tussles with exhausted fighting?

indicators.note: clumsy handling scrambles things, so these letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, so the word loses its insides and only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of fighting

explanation.surface: Awkward scraps between fighters who have run out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: clumsy brawls between tired fighters are exactly what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is a fight, especially a boxing match, of heavy, wild punches traded with little skill or defence.

clue.text: Willing fellow doffs cap

indicators.note: doffing a cap removes the head covering, so the word loses its top letter

parts.note: chappy is a familiar word for a chap or fellow

explanation.surface: An obliging man politely tips his hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy can mean willing or glad to do something, as in happy to help.

clue.text: Tasks former monarch to appear on South African money

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the late Queen
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: The duties of a late queen include appearing on South African banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Errands are small jobs or trips done for someone, so they are chores or tasks.

clue.text: Public showings of some sex positions

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Exhibitions that display some sexual positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Expos are exhibitions or trade fairs, events where things are put on view to the public.

clue.text: Criticises male dog charging in front of settee

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of settee
M is the abbreviation for male
a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a male dog for charging in front of the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: M and PUG charge into IN plus S, giving I-MPUG-NS.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim or person is to challenge or attack it verbally, so impugns means criticises.

clue.text: Concerned with Ford van being shifted?

parts.note: in can mean involved in or concerned in
the Transit is Ford's best-known van

explanation.surface: Somebody is worried about a Ford van being moved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Transit is a van, very common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in transit are being carried from one place to another, so they are being moved.

clue.text: Innovator's joke in seaside-entertainment spot?

parts.note: a pier at a British resort has arcades and shows
a joke, as in have you heard the one about

explanation.walkthrough: British seaside piers traditionally host comedy shows and amusements.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to explore or develop something new, so an innovator.

clue.text: Trumpet legend from Liege, lips in action

parts.note: the letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A legendary trumpeter from the Belgian city of Liège, his lips at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Dizzy Gillespie was a famous American jazz trumpeter; he was not from Liège, which is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy Gillespie was a bebop pioneer and one of the greatest jazz trumpeters, hence a legend.

clue.text: Bishop's office welcomes priest for binge

indicators.note: welcoming a guest means letting them inside, so the office word holds the priest

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese or office
PR is an abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A bishop's office hosts a priest for a bout of excess.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bout of unrestrained activity such as drinking or spending, like a binge.

clue.text: Top meal excludes seconds

indicators.note: to exclude something is to leave it out, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A first-rate dinner that leaves no room for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' suggests second helpings at the meal, but it is just the abbreviation S, removed from SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper and top are both adjectives for the higher of two positions, as in the upper or top deck.

clue.text: Worker pinching barrel after work held back eg Cooper's stock-in-trade?

indicators.note: after places the worker piece behind the reversed work piece in the answer
holding something back pulls it the wrong way, so this word is read in reverse

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: to pinch something is to grip it, so the worker word holds another letter inside

parts.note: a toiler is someone who works hard
B is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: A cooper, a barrel maker, has a worker pinching a barrel from his stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Cooper looks like the barrel maker, but it is Jilly Cooper, the British novelist of racy bestsellers. OP reversed is PO, then T(B)OILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a novel written quickly for money and mass appeal, the kind of popular fiction Jilly Cooper is known for.

clue.text: Slippery sort of mendacious salesman cleared out counterfeit rings

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the last word goes around the others

parts.note: first part of a word for counterfeit
mendacious means given to lying

parts.note: the first and last letters of salesman
rest of a word for counterfeit

explanation.surface: A slippery, dishonest salesman has been cleaned out by fake jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: FAKE, for counterfeit, rings LYING and SN. 'Slippery sort' sounds like a description of the salesman, but it defines the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying snake is a tree snake that glides through the air, and any snake is a slippery creature.

clue.text: First Lady's flat unfinished

indicators.note: something unfinished is missing its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: flat and level, as in an even surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, and flat an apartment; here flat means level.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Eve was the first woman created, so she is literally the first lady.

clue.text: Pursuing brilliant French novelist, high priests flag

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so these letters are reeling about in a new order

parts.note: star as an adjective means outstanding
George Sand was a French novelist
the seven letters of priests rearranged

explanation.surface: Priests on drugs chase after a brilliant French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand was the pen name of the 19th-century French novelist Aurore Dupin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the popular name for the national flag of the United States.

clue.text: For the meantime, intend checking fake Tinder

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so the intend word restrains the other letters inside it
something fake is not the genuine article, so the letters are given a false arrangement

parts.note: first letter of aim, which means intend
the letters of Tinder rearranged
rest of aim

explanation.surface: For now, I mean to stop a bogus profile on the dating app Tinder.
explanation.walkthrough: AIM, for intend, holds the rearranged TINDER. Tinder is the dating app.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad interim is Latin for in the interim, describing an arrangement that lasts only for the meantime.

clue.text: Identify people — recognise bloke holding another up

parts.note: to see can mean to recognise
a bloke is a man
another bloke

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' could attach to 'another' alone, but it reverses the whole assembly, so both men end up reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To name names is an idiom for revealing the identities of those involved, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Doubted fickle pseuds etc.

parts.note: the letters of pseuds and etc rearranged

explanation.surface: Changeable pretentious types and the like were not trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: A pseud is British slang for a pretentious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to suspect a person is to have misgivings about their honesty or truthfulness.

clue.text: Mock oath adapted by Mr and Mrs with ties around colony

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on either side of the colony word

parts.note: taken as written
the titles taken as written
taken as written
a hive houses a colony of bees

explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder. The rearranged letters wrap around HIVE: S-HIVE-RMYTIMBERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiver my timbers is the stock exclamation of fictional pirates, a comic, pretend curse rather than a real one.

clue.text: Unmasked journalist ushered in by 4

parts.note: the answer to 4 down
ED is short for editor

explanation.definitionFit: To be exposed is to have one's secret or true identity revealed, the same as being unmasked.

clue.text: Animosity about Sterne novel characterised by halting dialogue?

explanation.definitionFit: Pinteresque describes drama in the style of Harold Pinter, known for pauses, menace and fragmented, broken conversation.

clue.text: Stops blowing top and relaxes

clue.text: Crammed too much into Sabbath day
